artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.title: Presbytery authority to remove censure of suspended or deposed teaching elder

matches.evidence: A new presbytery may remove censures of suspension or deposition only with the original presbytery's permission or after satisfying BCO 37-7 procedures; the original presbytery retains recourse under BCO 40-3 through 40-5.

artifacts.title: Presbytery jurisdiction and restoration path for a deposed and repentant minister

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that restoration of a deposed minister follows BCO 37-4 and 37-7 exclusively, and BCO 18–21 ordination procedures do not apply.

artifacts.title: Ordination status and restoration process after deposition from office

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that a deposed officer has no ordination status, and restoration requires at minimum reaffirmation of vows, laying on of hands, and a proper call.

artifacts.title: Elevating a censure without a new trial under BCO 36

matches.evidence: Proposed amendment to BCO 36 providing for censure elevation without a wholly new trial was found to be ambiguous under the BCO.

artifacts.title: Restricting removal of excommunication to the original court

matches.evidence: An overture requiring only the original session to remove excommunication conflicted with BCO 37-7, which allows a court with current jurisdiction to act after a member relocates.
